Thanks for sending the draft. Two quick asks from our side as we move toward final:

2) Pen-test windows: we generally provide a 45-day notice window and prefer a quarterly schedule rather than ad-hoc inspections. Can Redwood propose language that balances our need to preserve production stability with your customer's audit requirements?

Subject: Consolidated redlines + proposed evidence tempo (MSA / Order Form)

Tom — thanks. I consolidated legal and security feedback and attached an MSA redline (MSA_Redline_v3.docx). High level suggestions below so your procurement team has a single working view: 

- SOC 2: Redwood will deliver SOC 2 Type II reports on an annual basis and provide a secure read-only link for customers within 10 business days of request. We propose adding a clause in the Security Exhibit that requires timely delivery but clarifies it is not a substitute for on-site inspections.

- Pen tests / Forensic access: propose a scoped inspection model — customers may request up to two inspection windows per 12 months with 45 days' notice. Live or privileged access requires a scoped runbook and an approved point of contact. For unannounced investigations (e.g., active incident), we propose a faster escalation path but only for agreed-to incident classes.

- Evidence cadence: recommended default cadence is: SOC 2 annual report (Type II), pen-test summary on request, and a quarterly verification checklist (status of remediations) via shared drive. This reduces repeated full inspections while giving confidence on controls.

Next steps: Laura (legal) — can you review the MSA redline where I flagged the inspection/notice language? Ben — please attach the order form worksheet with the evidence items we need to populate.

I attached: MSA_Redline_v3.docx (redline), OrderForm_Attachments_List.xlsx (evidence checklist).

Best,
Markus

Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — good consolidation. A few legal clarifications I suggest for the MSA redline: 

- Limit scope of "inspection" to operational systems relevant to the contracted services and exclude developer-level access or source code review. Language: "Inspection rights shall be limited to operational access to the Services necessary to validate compliance with the Security Exhibit and shall not include source code or internal development artifacts."

- Business hours / notice: require inspections to be scheduled during Redwoods' published maintenance windows where possible and to avoid high-impact production hours; where a customer requests an out-of-window inspection, Redwood will evaluate operational risk and may require mitigation steps or limitations.

- Data handling during evidence requests: add a clause that prohibits export or exfiltration of customer or Redwood production data during security reviews; forensic evidence can be provided in redacted/aggregated form unless there is a lawful basis or incident escalation that requires full access.

SOC2 delivery: Clearwell, please provide the secure link to the SOC2 Type II artifact and designate an operational contact for evidence requests. We will add a short Service Attachment to the Order Form to capture the evidence items and delivery timelines.

I made three inline edits in the MSA_Redline_v3.docx (highlighted) — see attached. Suggest we lock the inspection cadence language and use the OrderForm_Attachments_List.xlsx as the source of truth for what will be delivered at signing.
